[b]Concerning Relations with Gythena and the WMW Company[/b]

The Gythenan Prime Minister, Gabriel Holder, has announced that the Gythenan government and WMW Company have come to an agreement. The following details of the trade deal have been released:

[i]Gythena will purchase 75 WMW-RODENT tanks to be shipped out into the harbor of Edilthorpe.[/i]

[b]The Energy Cooperation Group[/b]

A brief session of the Standing Committee of the Categorization Bureau would go over the request of the Republic of Tartakum. The Social-Radical Party, Qianxuns minor party that specializes in foreign affairs, would ultimately conclude that Tartakum was ... geopolitically vulnerable... with an abundance of natural resources... requiring only some manner of guided leadership to pursue excellence. and would recommend the Foreign Affairs Committee of the MZP Central Committee to accept the request for close cooperation. A few hours later, Foreign Affairs too would accept the arrangement, empowering the Central State Commission to make provision for relations with Tartakum.

In a press release, Premier Liang Renshi would announce that the construction of the new oil rig in Tartakum would fall into the hands of the Project 661 Directorate under Director-General Kang Hongxin, whose faculty has had plenty of experience conducting seismic surveys of potential oil sources and constructing drill ships for oil collection. The Department of Oceanography would be assigned to this task, to be done in conjunction with the Department of Chemistry for logistical and material support. A temporary corporate organization called 能源合作集团 (Energy Cooperation Group) would be formed by the Directorate to oversee the construction of the oil rigs, with Kang Hongxin serving as its first chairman and president.

On the topic of the armament and training of Tartakums armed forces, Qianxun would be more hesitant, with conservative and nationalist members in the Min Zhu Partys Weilai clique cautioning general secretary Cui Fang against empowering an unproven nation. In the end though, Cui would partially accept some of Tartakums requests, directing SummitONE Solutions and Qunarco to establish a procurement contract with the Red Army Commission to aid in the manufacture of new armored military vehicles and small arms to the Tartakum armed forces. Qianxuns primary export vehicles, the ZSL-10 APC and the ZTZ-18 main battle tank, are expected to be primary objects of interest. Though, given Tartakums limited national budget, the antiquated ZTZ-65 main battle tank could also be considered for sale, with Qianxun maintaining a substantial reserve inventory in its university lands.

The training of Tartakums armed forces, however, would be deferred for now, with the Socialist Ethics Commission warning the MZP Central Committee that Tartakums receptiveness towards socialism could not be ascertained at the present time. Thus, Cui would instead ask that the Tartakum government prioritize the construction of embassies between the two nations first and the completion of all their prior transactions before they can move towards joint-training exercises. In the mean time, the Socialist Ethics Commission would send for agents to Tartakum to conduct field investigations so as to determine where its general populace stands on communism, whether the state permits the operation of left-wing political parties, and other quantities.
